confirmed: Source version verified: journal article by Eric Zhou and Dokyun Lee, PNAS Nexus 3(3), pgae052, published March 5, 2024. Independently read the complete Europe PMC full-text XML (PMC10914360; https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10914360/fullTextXML) and all 24 pages of pgae052_supplementary_data.pdf in memory from the supplementaryFiles API. No local main-article PDF or markdown is recorded in retrieval.json.

The observational design, observational context class, and exclusion from the randomized core are correct. Adoption is inferred from users' first known AI-generated posts; the event-study compares adopters with never-treated and not-yet-treated users. SI random assignments occur in sensitivity simulations on existing records, not an experiment assigning people to AI (main article, Materials and methods, Identifying AI adopters; SI pp. 2-4, Sections 1B and 2A; pp. 10 and 12, Sections 3C-3D).

The source reports over 53,000 users, over 4.3 million artworks, and over 5,800 known adopters, January 2022-June 2023. After winsorizing, Table S1 lists 4,764 adopters and 40,275 non-adopters. These are user counts and exceed 50; no people were randomized (SI p. 2, Section 1A and Table S1).

The novelty computation uses all adopters' artworks and a random sample of 10,000 control users; this random sampling is not randomized AI assignment. The panel is aggregated monthly. The 43,126 Content Novelty, 44,078 Visual Novelty, and 195,632 Value observations recorded in n_units are user-month observations, not distinct people; outcome-specific unique-user counts are not supplied by those tables (SI pp. 2-3, Sections 1A and 1C; pp. 16-19, Tables S6-S9).

The output measures and tools are correctly described: BLIP-2 captions with a Sentence-BERT embedding model for Content Novelty, DINOv2 embeddings for Visual Novelty, expanding prior-artwork reference sets, and favorites per view after 2 weeks for Value (main article, Materials and methods and Results, Creative value; SI p. 3, Sections 1C-1E).

S1-O1 matches the PDF: original aggregate ATT -0.0088; month 0 -0.0059* (SE 0.0019), month 6 -0.0161* (SE 0.0028), month 7 -0.0066 (SE 0.0036); observations 43,126 (SI p. 10, Table S4; p. 17, Table S7).

S1-O2 matches the PDF: original aggregate ATT 0.0032; month 1 0.0033* (SE 0.0011), month 6 0.0033 (SE 0.0021); observations 43,126. The quoted description of marginal statistical significance is present in the main text (SI p. 10, Table S4; p. 18, Table S8; main article, Results, Content Novelty).

S1-O3 matches the PDF: original aggregate ATT -0.0409; month -1 -0.0150* (SE 0.0033), month 0 -0.0286* (SE 0.0038), month 7 -0.1031* (SE 0.0083); observations 44,078 (SI p. 10, Table S4; p. 17, Table S7).
S1-O4 matches the PDF: original aggregate ATT -0.0048; month 0 -0.0039* (SE 0.0012), month 7 -0.0145* (SE 0.0030); observations 44,078 (SI p. 10, Table S4; p. 19, Table S9).

S1-O5 matches the sources: original aggregate ATT 0.0019; month 6 0.0092* (SE 0.0015); observations 195,632. The article reports a 50% increase by the sixth month, from a preadoption 2% to 3% favorites-per-view rate (SI p. 10, Table S4; p. 16, Table S6; main article, Results, Creative value).

All numerical claims and directions in one_line_finding match Table S4 and the main article's Fig. 1 discussion. Table S4's original ATTs aggregate group-period treatment effects within this observational study; they are not pooled study effects or standardized effect sizes (SI p. 10, Section 3C, Equation 3 and Table S4).
This is not a synthesis; leaving synthesis fields at their defaults is correct (main article, Introduction and Results).
summary: This is an observational study of self-selected AI adoption, with no randomized study of people. All recorded estimates and the one-line finding match the sources, but the form omits productivity and minimum-novelty results, available-statistics metadata, and the stated data/code archive links.
